create.name: Brother Phap Luu
create.bio:
Brother Phap Luu is a monk in Thich Nhat Hanh's Plum Village community. He became a novice in December 2003, took full ordination as a bhikshu three years later, and in 2011 received the Lamp Transmission from Thay, which authorised him to teach as a Dharma teacher. His home monastery is Deer Park in southern California, where he mentors younger monks, teaches the sutras and the monastic code, and shares in the daily work of the community.

Much of his teaching has been aimed at young people and at education. He helped organise Wake Up tours that brought mindfulness practice to university students in the United States, Britain and Spain, and he works with the Wake Up Schools programme, hoping to make simple practices such as conscious breathing and caring for strong emotions part of schooling at every level. He has also been involved in the Happy Farm project at Upper Hamlet in France, which joins organic farming with community life and practice. He gives Dharma talks in English, French and Spanish; recorded talks range over the Diamond Sutra, the Four Noble Truths, emotions, fear and climate change, and a long online class series on core tenets of the Plum Village teaching.

free_resources.title: Class series: Plum Village Looks at Vulture's Peak (Class #1)
free_resources.description: The first of a series of recorded evening classes in which Brother Phap Luu works through the tenets of a book by Thich Nhat Hanh, one tenet per class. Free to watch in the Plum Village library.

free_resources.title: The Diamond Sutra: The Practice of Signlessness
free_resources.description: A recorded Dharma talk on the Diamond Sutra and the practice of looking beyond signs and appearances. Free in the Plum Village online library.

free_resources.title: Understanding the Nature of Suffering
free_resources.description: A recorded Dharma talk on how suffering arises and how practice helps us look into it. Free in the Plum Village online library.
